description: The line plot illustrates the time cost (in seconds) required to process an increasing number of academic papers, comparing two system configurations: one without pre-computation (blue line) and one with pre-computation (orange line). The x-axis, labeled “Paper Number,” uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 256, with tick marks at powers of two (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256). The y-axis, labeled “Time Cost (s),” uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 35 seconds, with major tick marks every 5 seconds. The blue line (“w/o Pre-computation”) starts near 1 second at 1 paper, rises gradually to about 3 seconds at 16 papers, then steepens sharply to approximately 9 seconds at 64 papers, and climbs rapidly to over 35 seconds at 256 papers. In contrast, the orange line (“w Pre-computation”) remains nearly flat across the entire range, staying consistently below 1 second — approximately 0.5 seconds — from 1 to 256 papers, indicating negligible time cost growth with increasing paper count.
